# Maester Packs that ship with Maester

Each folder here is a [Maester Pack](https://maester.dev/docs/packs) that is part of the Maester module:
a `maester-pack.json`, its suites of native tests, and its helpers and connectors.

- The build copies this folder to `packs/` in the module. A pack loads into its own private module from
  its folder; it is not compiled into `Maester.psm1`.
- A pack here is trusted as the module is: it needs no lock entry and no approval. It runs when its
  manifest says `"EnabledByDefault": true` unless the Maester config turns it off with
  `Packs: [{ "Id": "<id>", "Enabled": false }]`, and the other way round.
- Its ID is `maester.<name>`. Its `Code` is its own, such as `ZTA`. Because it is part of Maester, its test IDs
  have no `MP.` prefix: they are `ZTA.<n>` (or `ZTA` for a family), and its suite IDs start with `ZTA`. The code
  is added to the reserved prefixes in `powershell/assets/MaesterTestSchema.psd1`, so custom tests cannot use it. A pack installed later may not take a code that overlaps it. Its rows in the results have `Source = Custom` and a `Package`, so they never count as
  Maester's own checks.
- PowerShell Gallery modules it declares in `Uses.Modules` are pinned to one version. Users save them with
  `Install-MtPack <id>`, which records each module's digest in `maester-packs.lock.json`.

Check a pack with `Test-MtPack ./packs/<name> -Official` and run its tests with `Invoke-MtTest -Path ./packs/<name>`.

input.recap: I've proposed a "1,254 checks" section for maester.dev, with real counts from the catalog and a rough history from git. Nothing is built yet. Two calls are still yours: whether community packs go into the catalog, and how the build refreshes daily.
input.ask: Should I build the shipped-checks part on the homepage now?

content.text:
The mockup above uses real numbers. Maester ships 890 built-in checks today. The Zero Trust Assessment pack, which ships in the module, adds 364 more. That makes 1,254 checks across 14 products and 124 ATT&CK techniques.

## What I'd put on the site

1. **One big number, with where it comes from: "1,254 checks you can run"**, split into built-in, packs that ship with Maester, and community packs. Showing the split is what makes the ecosystem argument: the core is large, and packs grow it further.
2. **A stacked area chart of checks over time**, with built-in tests at the bottom and packs layered on top. Mark the releases (1.0, 2.0, 3.0). As community packs appear they become the top layer, so the chart shows the ecosystem growing, not just the module.
3. **A breakdown of checks by product**, to show breadth. It also shows what packs add: most Azure and Purview checks come from the pack, not the core. This could link straight into the catalog explorer, filtered to that product.

Put the number and the growth chart on the homepage. Put the product breakdown at the top of the test catalog.

## Should the catalog include packs?

**Packs that ship with Maester: they're already in.** `catalog-explorer.mjs` already reads `catalog.Packs`, so ZTA's 364 tests are in the explorer. We only need to count them in the headline.

**Community packs: yes, but don't count them as Maester's own.**
- Get them from the packs.maester.dev index (the Worker API in the Packs design). The site build shouldn't crawl GitHub.
- Label each one with its pack and publisher badge, the same way pack results carry `Source = Custom`.
- Leave them out of framework coverage and the "built-in" number.

**Daily updates: yes, for the community layer only.**
- The site already rebuilds on every merge to main, so built-in counts stay current.
- Add a daily scheduled run of the build-website workflow that fetches the pack index.

**History needs two sources:**
- **Built-in:** work it out from git, counting at each release tag. Nothing needs storing, so it fits the rule against committing generated website data.
- **Community packs:** they can disappear from GitHub, and per the earlier ruling we never cache their repos, so git can't rebuild their history. Have the indexer write one row a day (date, pack, test count) to D1 and serve it from the API.

## Two things to settle before it goes live

- **Shims could count one check twice.** If a CIS shim and the MT test it calls both count, we're counting one setting twice. 53 ZTA tests also list `AlsoCheckedBy` built-in tests. I'd show the headline as total checks and give the distinct-settings figure in a tooltip. That way nobody can say the number is inflated.
- **The history before 3.0 in the mockup is rough.** I counted test names in the old Pester files, which misses tests whose names are built from variables. That likely explains part of the jump from 477 to 890 at 3.0. Before publishing, I'd backfill properly by running Pester discovery at each release tag, once, and saving the result.

---
name: catalog-growth-showcase
description: maester.dev "how many checks" showcase — owner rulings 2026-11-08 on counting shims, community packs in the catalog, daily refresh
metadata:
  type: project
---

Owner rulings (2026-11-08) for the maester.dev section that sells the size of the check collection (headline count, growth chart, checks by product):

- **Count every test as unique by default.** Shims and pack tests with `AlsoCheckedBy` are counted separately. A toggle may group them for a "distinct checks" count, but only as a toggle, never the default.
- **Community packs go in the test catalog**, so there is one place to discover checks, but each is clearly highlighted as coming from a community pack (not Maester's own).
- Built-in history is derived from git per release tag; community-pack history can't be (no repo caching, see [[maester-marketplace-design]]), so it needs daily snapshots from the packs index.

**Why:** the section is a selling point for the ecosystem; the count must look big but stay defensible.

**How to apply:** keep the default count ungrouped; label community-pack rows/badges distinctly in the explorer.

### Making one with an AI image tool

Any image tool that takes a text prompt can make a banner. Image tools often misspell words, so check every letter,
or ask for an image with no text and add the title yourself in an editor. Fill in the parts in angle brackets:

```text
A wide banner image, 1200 x 630 pixels, for a software add-on called "<pack name>".
It checks the security settings of <service, for example Google Workspace> for IT administrators.
Style: clean, modern, flat illustration on a <dark navy / deep teal / near-black> gradient background,
with a simple abstract motif suggesting <what the pack checks, for example identity, email, devices>.
Text: the title "<pack name>" in large, bold, white sans-serif letters on the left,
and the line "<one short phrase, at most six words>" below it in smaller letters.
Leave a margin of at least 60 pixels on every side. No other text, no logos, no people,
no photos of screens, no badges or seals.
```

For an image without text, replace the `Text:` line with `No text at all; leave the left half plain for a title.`

## The pack page

Every pack's page on [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud) has the same sections: Install, Connect,
Run, App-only, Tests, Security and Support. The index fills what it can from the manifest:

- the modules in `Uses.Modules`, with the line that installs each one;
- the Graph permissions in `Uses.GraphScopes`, which an app needs to run the pack app-only;
- the tests, with their products, from `Suites` (and `Catalog` for a family test that expands when it runs).

The rest comes from the Guide, a JSON file in the pack named by the manifest's `Guide` key, such as
`"Guide": "maester-pack.guide.json"`. Its schema is
[maester-pack-guide-1.0.json](https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-guide-1.0.json); add it as `$schema` so
editors check the file as you type. Commands in it are shown as text and never run. A short example:

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://maester.dev/schemas/maester-pack-guide-1.0.json",
  "Summary": "Checks the security settings of Google Workspace.",
  "Prerequisites": [{ "Text": "A Google Workspace super admin account." }],
  "Connect": { "Steps": [{ "Text": "Connect Maester, then sign in to Google when asked", "Command": "Connect-Maester" }] },
  "Run": {
    "Commands": [{ "Text": "Only this pack", "Command": "Invoke-Maester -Pack CNT -SkipBuiltIn" }],
    "Options": [{ "Name": "GoogleWorkspace.Customer", "Default": "my_customer", "Text": "The customer ID to read." }]
  },
  "AppOnly": { "Supported": true, "Methods": { "Certificate": true, "ClientSecret": true }, "Text": "Use a service account key." },
  "Screenshots": [{ "Path": "assets/report.png", "Caption": "The pack's results in the Maester report" }],
  "Support": { "Pack": "https://github.com/contoso/maester-google-workspace/issues" }
}
```

Maester checks that the Guide is a JSON object and that its screenshots (at most six) are `.png`, `.jpg` or `.webp`
paths inside the pack. Like the banner, a screenshot that really is an image of at most 1 MB is not counted as
binary content. Any section can end with `"More": "<https link>"` to your own documentation. The
[Zero Trust Assessment pack's guide](https://github.com/maester365/maester/blob/main/packs/zero-trust-assessment/maester-pack.guide.json)
is a full example.

# Maester Packs index

The site and index behind [packs.maester.cloud](https://packs.maester.cloud): the list of Maester Packs, a page per pack
with its tests, connector and security scan, and the `index.json`, `codes.json` and `blocklist.json` that
`Find-MtPack` and Maester read. The design is section 7 and 8 of the Maester Packs design (maester365/maester#2396).

```
data/       sources.json (extra repositories to index); seed/ holds the starting reserved codes, blocklist, official and
            featured lists, which `npm run db:seed` copies into D1. After that, admins manage them on /admin
            sample/ is a built index of the packs in fixtures/, so the site builds and CI runs without the network
indexer/    Invoke-PackIndex.ps1: fetches, validates and scans every pack with Maester's own checks
site/       the static site (Astro), built from the index
worker/     the Cloudflare Worker: install events, Maester's run telemetry, usage counts and the scan queue, at /api/v1/*
```

## How a pack gets listed

1. Someone runs `Install-MtPack owner/repo`. Maester posts an install event to `/api/v1/events`, which queues the
   repository. Its status page then says what is needed to list it.
2. Every ten minutes the **Index** workflow's `scan` job reads the queue, downloads each pack at its latest release
   and runs Maester's `Test-MtPackContent` on it. Nothing in a pack runs. The job has no secrets and a read-only token.
3. The index applies its own rules: the repository must be public (private and internal ones are never listed), the
   pack must be published on the site (below), the blocklist, a 30-day minimum owner account age, duplicate content
   and a tagged release.
4. The `publish` job writes the result to the `listings` branch, builds the site, bundles both Workers and writes them
   to the `deploy` branch, which Cloudflare deploys (see Deploying below).

**The pack registry.** A pack is listed only after an admin of its repository signs in at /account and presses
Publish. The Worker checks the repository is public and registers the manifest's `Guid` and `Code` to the repository's
owner (by GitHub ID). From then on the Guid keeps that code and owner for good, and nobody else can publish that code,
even if the repository is made private or deleted. A release that changes the code for a registered Guid is not listed
(`CodeChanged`): the publisher goes back, or gives the pack a new Guid. A release of a published pack that changes
its Guid but keeps its code is not listed either (`GuidChanged`): the publisher sets the Guid back. A copied manifest
is refused (`GuidTaken`), as is a registered or reserved code (`CodeTaken`). Only an admin can remove a registration, on /admin.

**Hiding a pack.** An admin of a pack's repository can hide it from the site for a while, on /account (My Packs),
and show it again there. The next index run leaves it out (`Hidden`) and its status page says why. Its Guid and code
stay registered to it, and Maester still installs it from its repository: hiding only takes it off the site.

**Page URLs.** A pack's page is `/p/{code}` (`/p/cnt`, `/p/cnt.gws`), with `/tests`, `/connector`, `/security` and
`/tests/{test id}` under it. The code is registered to the pack for good, so the URL survives a repository rename,
move or transfer and links to it keep working. Publishers are at `/publishers/{owner}`; status pages, which also cover
packs that are not listed and may have no code yet, stay at `/status/{owner}/{repo}`.

## Usage and telemetry

Maester sends its telemetry to `https://api.maester.dev`, a second Worker (`worker/wrangler.api.toml`, `worker/src/api.ts`)
with no site files that answers only `POST /v1/telemetry` and `POST /v1/events`, so an admin can allow or block
telemetry without touching the site, and the site stays static-first. It runs the same handlers against the same
stores as the site's Worker. The
same endpoints stay at `/api/v1/*` on packs.maester.cloud. While this is proven, `Invoke-Maester` also sends its old
PostHog event. It posts two events to `/v1/telemetry`. A `start` event goes when a run begins, and a `run` event when it ends, completed or not.
A start with no run means the run crashed or hung. They carry:

- a random run ID and installation ID, and a SHA-256 hash of the tenant ID, which the Worker re-keys with the
  `TENANT_KEY` secret before storing it (tenant IDs are public, so a plain hash could be matched by guessing);
- the Maester and PowerShell versions, the OS, its version and architecture, and the CI system if any;
- when the run started and how long it took;
- the outcome. A run that is `Incomplete` also has the stage it reached and the .NET type of the last error;
- the result counts;
- the public packs installed, and the public or built-in packs that ran.

A private pack is never sent. The Worker adds the country, region and continent from Cloudflare and does not store the IP
address. `-DisableTelemetry` or `MAESTER_DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` turns all of it off, including the install event.

Each event goes to three stores:

| Store | Binding | Holds | Kept | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Analytics Engine | `RUNS` | every event, plus one point per pack run or installed | about 90 days | dashboards and failure alerts; SQL API, Grafana |
| Pipelines → R2 | `RUN_STREAM` | every event as a row (schema in `worker/pipeline-schema.json`) | until deleted | long-term analysis with DuckDB or any Parquet reader |
| D1 | `DB` | run events, as one row per installation and day | 400 days | the site's counts and the report endpoint |
| D1 | `DB` | `daily_*` totals with no installation, tenant or network | for good | trends over years, `/api/v1/history` |

**Daily totals.** So trends reach back years after the per-installation rows are deleted, D1 keeps small daily tables
that hold no installation, tenant or network. The Worker adds to four of them as each event arrives:

| Table | One row per day and | Counts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `daily_events` | event type, Maester version, OS, CI, outcome, stage | events, test and result sums, total duration and how many runs reported one |

﻿<#
    .SYNOPSIS
    Exports the built-in Maester test catalog to JSON for the website test-docs generator.

    .DESCRIPTION
    Imports the Maester module from source (powershell/Maester.psd1), reads every built-in native test
    with Get-MtTest and writes its metadata to a JSON file. website/scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs reads
    that file, plus each test's Test.<ID>.md, to build the test pages of the website.

    Each test has its attributes (Product, RelatedProduct, Feature, Area and ResourceType as taxonomy keys),
    the derived Block, Suite and Source, and LegacyTag: the tags it carried in Maester 2.x, which -Tag still
    matches. Taxonomy at the top level gives the display names of the keys and ATT&CK techniques the tests use.

    A test of a suite that implements a published benchmark also has Benchmark, from the framework file of its
    suite (tests/<suite>/frameworks/<key>.json): Framework, Version, Requirement and the requirement's own
    facts, such as the CIS level and profiles. Its Control lists the controls of other frameworks that the
    requirement relates to. Benchmark is null for every other test. Frameworks at the top level gives the Name,
    Version and Url of each framework by Key.

    Packs lists the packs that ship with Maester (packs/<name>/maester-pack.json) with the tests of their catalog,
    such as the Zero Trust Assessment's, so the site can show them beside the built-in checks. The Taxonomy names
    the keys and techniques that the packs' tests use as well.

    No tenant connection is needed and no test code is run. Importing the module requires
    Microsoft.Graph.Authentication to be installed (it is a RequiredModule of Maester).

    The output is deterministic: tests are sorted by ID (ordinal, case-insensitive), paths are
    repository-relative with forward slashes, and the file is UTF-8 without BOM with LF line endings.

    .PARAMETER OutputPath
    Where to write the JSON file. Defaults to website/src/data/test-catalog.json, the catalog the website builds from.

    .EXAMPLE
    ./build/docs/Export-MtTestCatalogForDocs.ps1

    Writes website/src/data/test-catalog.json. The website's build turns it into the test pages; `npm run
    export-catalog` (in website/) runs this script.
#>
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [Parameter()]
    [string] $OutputPath
)

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$repoRoot = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path -Path $PSScriptRoot -ChildPath '..' -AdditionalChildPath '..')).Path
if (-not $OutputPath) { $OutputPath = Join-Path -Path $repoRoot -ChildPath 'website' -AdditionalChildPath 'src', 'data', 'test-catalog.json' }

Import-Module (Join-Path -Path $repoRoot -ChildPath 'powershell' -AdditionalChildPath 'Maester.psd1') -Force -WarningAction SilentlyContinue

function ConvertTo-RepoPath {
    param([string] $Path)
    if (-not $Path) { return '' }
    $full = [System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath($Path)
    return [System.IO.Path]::GetRelativePath($repoRoot, $full).Replace('\', '/')
}

function ConvertTo-StringArray {
    param($Value)
    return , @(@($Value) | Where-Object { $null -ne $_ -and "$_" -ne '' } | ForEach-Object { "$_" })
}

$tests = @(Get-MtTest | Where-Object { $_.BuiltIn })
$invalid = @($tests | Where-Object { -not $_.IsValid })
if ($invalid.Count -gt 0) {
    $list = ($invalid | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Id): $(@($_.Errors | ForEach-Object { $_.Message ?? "$_" }) -join '; ')" }) -join [Environment]::NewLine
    throw "Get-MtTest reported $($invalid.Count) invalid built-in test(s):$([Environment]::NewLine)$list"
}

$comparer = [System.StringComparer]::OrdinalIgnoreCase
$sorted = [System.Linq.Enumerable]::ToArray([System.Linq.Enumerable]::OrderBy([object[]]$tests, [Func[object, string]] { param($t) $t.Id }, $comparer))

$module = Get-Module Maester
$catalog = foreach ($t in $sorted) {
    [ordered]@{
        Id                 = $t.Id
        Title              = $t.Title
        Suite              = $t.Suite
        Source             = $t.Source
        Block              = $t.Block
        Product            = if ($t.Product) { "$($t.Product)" } else { '' }
        RelatedProduct     = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.RelatedProduct
        Feature            = if ($t.Feature) { "$($t.Feature)" } else { '' }
        Area               = if ($t.Area) { "$($t.Area)" } else { '' }
        ResourceType       = if ($t.ResourceType) { "$($t.ResourceType)" } else { '' }
        Severity           = $t.Severity
        UserImpact         = if ($t.UserImpact) { "$($t.UserImpact)" } else { '' }
        ImplementationCost = if ($t.ImplementationCost) { "$($t.ImplementationCost)" } else { '' }
        Mitre              = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.Mitre
        Control            = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.Control
        Benchmark          = $t.Benchmark
        Service            = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.Service
        License            = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.License
        Permission         = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.Permission
        Lifecycle          = "$($t.Lifecycle)"
        ReplacedBy         = if ($t.ReplacedBy) { "$($t.ReplacedBy)" } else { '' }
        LongRunning        = [bool]$t.LongRunning
        InstanceSource     = if ($t.InstanceSource) { "$($t.InstanceSource)" } else { '' }
        Tag                = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.Tag
        LegacyTag          = ConvertTo-StringArray (& $module { param($test) (Get-MtSelectionTag -Test $test).Legacy } $t)
        Author             = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.Author
        Contributor        = ConvertTo-StringArray $t.Contributor
        HelpUrl            = if ($t.HelpUrl) { "$($t.HelpUrl)" } else { '' }
        FunctionName       = $t.FunctionName
        File               = ConvertTo-RepoPath $t.File
        MarkdownPath       = ConvertTo-RepoPath $t.MarkdownPath
    }
}

import json,subprocess,re,collections
cat=json.load(open('website/src/data/test-catalog.json'))
prod={t['Id']:t['Product'] for t in cat['Tests']}
ex=json.load(open('website/src/data/explorer.json'))
tags=[('v0.1','2024-06'),('0.2.0','2024-07'),('0.3.0','2024-08'),('1.0.0','2024-12'),('1.1.0','2025-05'),('1.2.0','2025-06'),('2.0.0','2025-12'),('2.1.0','2026-05'),('2.2.0','2026-07'),('2.3.0','2026-10')]
rows=[]
for tag,d in tags:
    out=subprocess.run(['git','grep','-h','-E','^[[:space:]]*It[[:space:]]',tag,'--','tests'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.splitlines()
    c=collections.Counter()
    for l in out:
        m=re.search(r'''It\s+["']([A-Za-z][\w-]*(?:\.[\w-]+)*)[:\s]''',l)
        p=prod.get(m.group(1)) if m else None
        if not p and m and m.group(1).startswith('MT1060'): p='entra'
        c[p or 'other']+=1
    rows.append((tag.lstrip('v'),d,dict(c)))
now=collections.Counter(t['product'] or 'other' for t in ex['tests'])
rows.append(('Today','2026-11',dict(now)))
tot=collections.Counter()
for r in rows: tot.update(r[2])

print(sorted(tot.items(),key=lambda x:-x[1]))

content.text:
The four chart options above all use real counts per release. I took the test IDs from each release in git and matched them to today's products. Early releases show some "Other" because a few old test IDs no longer exist.

- **A, smooth stacked area:** the top edge is the headline total and each band is a product. It's the closest to what you asked for, and my pick.
- **B, streamgraph:** looks the most organic, but you can't read exact totals off it.
- **C, 100% stacked:** shows how the mix spread from mostly Entra to Active Directory, Intune and Defender.
- **D, small multiples:** one small chart per product, all on the same scale.

Option C or D would work as a second view next to A. Whichever you pick, it will replace the current jagged chart and the product bars, and use smooth curves.

- **Homepage:** a new section counts 1,872 checks: 890 built in, 364 from the Zero Trust Assessment pack and 618 from community packs. Each test counts once by default. - **Test catalog:** community pack checks are listed with the rest, with a violet "Community pack" badge, and link to their page on packs.maester.cloud. The sidebar has a "Community packs" group.
- **Data:** each build reads the community packs and counts the checks in every past release from git. The existing daily build picks up new packs.

**Before community checks appear on maester.dev:**
- **The packs site needs to publish a list of checks.** I added a `catalog.json` file (every listed pack with its tests) to packs.maester.cloud, in `jozrahq/maester-cloud-packs` on branch `feat/catalog-json`. - **Colour by product**: built-in tiles are full colour and pack tiles are lighter.
- Hovering a tile names it and gives its count. On the site, clicking a tile would open the catalog filtered to that product and suite or pack.

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: - Show on maester.dev how large and varied the collection of checks is, as a selling point for the ecosystem. Count the out-of-box tests plus the tests in all Maester packs, including community packs. Show it with a chart, such as checks over time. - Include community packs in the test catalog so there is one place to discover checks, while highlighting that they come from a community pack. Update the data daily. - User rulings, in order: - Count each test as unique by default. A grouping toggle was first allowed only as a toggle; the user later asked to remove it entirely. - The growth chart must be smooth. - No treemap. Keep the original product bars ("the other one was better"). - Remove the long run-command note about community packs. - Move community packs to the bottom of all lists. - Fix the homepage section's missing padding. - In the Source filter, group packs under a "Maester Packs" heading instead of repeating "community". - Fix the chart's proportions (white space below it). - Remove the intro text on the All checks page. - Remove "It never buys a say in what a check reports." from the homepage. - Latest: in the sponsors text, say we're thankful, that Maester 3.0 and the future of Maester are possible because of sponsors, and add "help us sustain and improve Maester for the community". - The user asked to "run the site so I can see it": the dev server is at http://localhost:3200. 2. Key Technical Concepts: - The maester.dev site is Astro + Starlight. - Generated data lives in `website/src/data/*.json` and is git-ignored. - `prepare-data.mjs` runs before dev and build. - `generate-test-docs.mjs` writes `explorer.json` and the pages under `.generated/tests`. - The packs index at packs.maester.cloud (internal repo `jozrahq/maester-cloud-packs`): - `index.json` is public and has per-pack test counts. - Per-test listings are on the internal `listings` branch. - I added a `catalog.json` route. - Built-in history comes from git release tags: - Pester `It` blocks before 3.0. - `Test.*.ps1` native test files from 3.0 on. - `packs/*/catalog.json` for the packs that ship with Maester. - The smooth chart uses monotone cubic interpolation (like curveMonotoneX), computed server-side in Astro into SVG paths. - The build-website workflow already rebuilds daily (cron "17 3 * * *"). - Rules from AGENTS.md: - Never commit generated website data. - Commit or push only when the user asks; if on the default branch, branch first. - Commit messages end with "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 ". - PR descriptions end with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)". 3. Files and Code Sections: - `website/scripts/community-packs.mjs` (new) - Fetches `${MAESTER_PACKS_URL ?? 'https://packs.maester.cloud'}/catalog.json`, falling back to `index.json` (counts only). - Drops packs with the `BuiltIn` badge. - Writes `src/data/community-packs.json` as `{source, generatedAt, packs:[{id, code, name, description, publisher, version, badges, products, url, count, tests:[{id, title, severity, product, pillar, category, url}]}]}`. - Exports `communityPacksPath` and `writeCommunityPacks`. - `website/scripts/catalog-history.mjs` (new) - Writes `src/data/catalog-history.json` as `{releases:[{version, date, builtIn, packs}]}` for stable tags, skipping 0.0.x through `isRelease`. - Current output starts at 0.1 (106 checks), then 2.2.0 (722) and 2.3.0 (751). - `website/scripts/prepare-data.mjs` - Runs community-packs.mjs and catalog-history.mjs when their output is missing (before the explorer). - Regenerates the explorer when community-packs.json was missing. - Header comment updated. - `website/scripts/catalog-explorer.mjs` - `writeExplorerData(catalog, releasedTests, contributors, community = { packs: [] })`. - Adds `communityPacks` and community tests (`community: true`, `url`, `pack: code`, `suite: code`). - Adds `community` to the totals. - Products get an `own` count and are sorted by `own` then count. - Tests are sorted with community last. - The `shimOf` field was removed. - `website/scripts/generate-test-docs.mjs` - Imports `communityPacksPath` and reads the file if it exists. - `renderRootIndex` intro text removed: the page body is now only an import comment and ``. - `website/src/components/catalog/data.ts` - `Check` type gains `community?`, `url?`. - Adds `communityPackOf`, `packName`, and `checkHref = (t) => t.url || checkUrl(t.id)`. - `website/src/components/catalog/CatalogList.astro` - Rows use `href={checkHref(t)}` and `data-community`. - Community rows get the badge "Community pack · CODE" (`.mt-cl__badge--community`, violet, with a dark variant). - Run command: community packs are excluded from `packs`. If only community rows are shown, the command is `Invoke-Maester -Pack X -SkipBuiltIn` with a short note to install the pack first. - Group ordering ranks by non-community row count (`own()`). - `website/src/components/catalog/CatalogNav.astro` - The "Community packs" `
` section sits after Suites. Each entry is an external link with the code chip `.mt-cnav__code--community`. - Source filter values: "Built into Maester", then the packs under a "Maester Packs" subheading (`v.heading`, rendered as `

`). Shipped packs come first, then community packs, listed by name. - `website/src/components/CatalogGrowth.astro` (new) - Section `

` with its own styles: max-width 75rem, padding 3.5rem 1rem, plus `.eyebrow` and `h2` rules copied from the page. - Content: - Heading: "1,872 checks, and more every release." - Intro: "From 106 checks in Maester 0.1 to 1,872 today: 17.7× in 2.4 years…". - Three source cards: 890 built in, 364 packs that ship with Maester, 618 community packs. - Smooth stacked chart: W=760, H=440, layers builtIn/shipped/community via the `curve()` monotone function. Fills use fill-opacity 0.16; lines are drawn top layer down. The end dot has a label. Colours: `--g-builtIn: var(--mt-ember)`, `--g-shipped: #2563eb`, `--g-community: #7c3aed`, via a `--layer` variable. - `.mt-growth__chart` is a flex column so the SVG fills the card. - Product bars: top 10 products, stacked segments by source. - The toggle, its script and all data-grouped attributes were removed. - `website/src/pages/index.astro` - Imports CatalogGrowth and explorer.json. - Stats band: `{format(builtIn + zta + community)}` with "Checks: N in Maester + N from community packs". - `` is placed before the Coverage section. - Removed the "Checks for the services you actually run" chips section and the `products` array. - Sponsors paragraph is now: "We're thankful to every sponsor: Maester 3.0, and the future of Maester, are possible because of them. Sponsorship pays for maintainer time and the test tenants every check is proven against. Become a sponsor to help us sustain and improve Maester for the community." - `.gitignore`: adds `website/src/data/community-packs.json` and `website/src/data/catalog-history.json`. - `AGENTS.md`: the hard-rule list of generated website data now includes community-packs.json and catalog-history.json, and mentions packs.maester.cloud. - `.github/workflows/build-website.yaml`: comments only; the daily run also picks up community packs. - `build/docs/Export-MtTestCatalogForDocs.ps1`: the ShimOf addition was reverted with `git checkout`, so the file is unchanged. - `~/github/maester-cloud-packs`, branch `feat/catalog-json`, commit a19cf54 (local, not pushed): - New `site/src/pages/catalog.json.ts` serving `{Version:1, GeneratedAt, Packs:[{Id, Code, Name, Description, Owner, Source, Version, Badges, Risk, Products, PublishedAt, Url, Tests:[{Id, Title, Severity, Product, Pillar, Category, Url}]}]}`. - README mention added. - Memory: - `memory/catalog-growth-showcase.md` (rulings) and its MEMORY.md line, updated after the toggle removal. 4. Errors and fixes: - Pester `It` counts per tag at first returned 0: `\s` isn't supported in git grep ERE, so I used `[[:space:]]`. - Early 0.0.x tags gave noisy counts, so they're excluded. - The d3 widget mockup rendered empty for the user (CDN), so I re-rendered it as pre-computed static SVG. - In the growth chart, line paths inherited the fill colour (CSS order), which filled huge wedges. Fixed with a `--layer` variable: `.mt-growth__fill{fill:var(--layer)}` and `.mt-growth__line{fill:none;stroke:var(--layer)}`. - The violet line overlapped the built-in line across history; fixed by drawing lines in reverse layer order. - The homepage section had no padding because index.astro styles are scoped; the component now has its own styles. - The chart left white space under it; fixed with H=440 and a flex-column figure. - My first Pester run was started detached and died. - I also briefly ran `git stash` while a run was going (careless); the changes were restored. - The final clean run: 7,066 of 7,071 passed. The 5 failures are in PublishedModuleResultDetail.Tests.ps1 because Test.MT.1181's `AGENT_365` licence is missing from this branch's licence table. It's already fixed on origin/main, so it's unrelated to this work. 5. Problem Solving: - Community per-test data isn't public on the live site until the `catalog.json` route is deployed. The local test used a packs-site build against the real listings branch (`MAESTER_PACKS_URL=http://localhost:4399`), so the local community-packs.json has the full 618 tests. - In production, before deploy, the fallback is counts only from index.json. 6. All user messages: - "In the maester site i want to show the variety and alreg collection of tests that we have as a selling point for maester. in it we should take the out of the box tests as well as the count of tests across all maester packs and show how rich a collection of tests that we have. this is to highlitht the value of the ecosystem. come up with a way how we can represent this. I think a chart that shows the tests over time (or anything else might be good). should we thinkig of including packs in our test catalog too and have it updated daily?" - "by default keep each one unique. we could add a toggle that says to group the shims and alsocheckedby so we get a more real count (but use that only as a toggle). lets include the community packs in the catalog so there is one place to discover but lets highlight they come from a community pack." - "I don't like the look of the chart. it needs to be alot smoother one. Can we do an area chart of the distrubution of charts for the products..." - "how me different mockups of the charts..." - (with images) "i actually prefer for the growth to show it smoothly. as for the second one. that is the one I want like an area chart like the one in the third, not sure what its called.. show me a mock" - "the mock chart is empty" - "lets remove the treemap. the other one was better." - "run the site so i can see it" - "in the test catalog don't show this long line int he home page 'Install the community packs first (…)…' also move the community packs to the bottom of all the lists. the home page is not showing any padding for the new chart" - "in the test catalog for Source insted of repeating the word community, group them under a Maester Pack heading and list the packs" - (image) "the chart is not proportional, there's white space below the line chart..." - "lets remove this toggle 'Count a setting once when several suites check it'" - "this is too much text '890 checks built into Maester, … install a pack with Install-MtPack to run its checks.' lets remove all that. no one wnats to know them." - "lets remove this from the home page ' It never buys a say in what a check reports.'" - "say something like we are thankful, Maester 3.0 and the future of Maester is possible because of them. Plus say help us sustain and improve maester for the community" 7. Pending Tasks: - Nothing is committed. All Maester changes are uncommitted on the unrelated branch `feat/report-compressed-data` and need their own branch, but only when the user asks. - The packs-site `feat/catalog-json` commit isn't pushed; push or deploy only when the user asks. 8. Current Work: - The latest request was to rewrite the homepage sponsors paragraph in `website/src/pages/index.astro`. I replaced it with: "We're thankful to every sponsor: Maester 3.0, and the future of Maester, are possible because of them. Sponsorship pays for maintainer time and the test tenants every check is proven against. Become a sponsor to help us sustain and improve Maester for the community." - I verified it on localhost:3200 by reading the text and taking a screenshot; it renders correctly under the heading "Maester is free because these sponsors pay for the work." - The closing message to the user, and wrap_up, haven't been sent yet. 9. ## What

Shows on maester.dev how large the collection of checks is, counting the built-in tests, the packs that ship with Maester and the community packs.

- **Homepage growth section** (`CatalogGrowth.astro`): a headline count, three source cards, a smooth stacked area chart of checks per release (built in / shipped packs / community packs) and bars for the top products. The stats band now includes community pack checks.
- **Test catalog**: community pack checks are listed beside Maester's own. Each has a "Community pack · CODE" badge, links to its pack's page on packs.maester.cloud, and sorts last. The Source filter groups the packs under a "Maester Packs" heading. The intro text on the All checks page is removed.
- **Sponsors text** thanks the sponsors who make Maester 3.0 and its future possible.

## Data

`prepare-data.mjs` writes two new generated files, both ignored by git (added to the AGENTS.md hard rule):

- `community-packs.json`, from `https://packs.maester.cloud/catalog.json`. Until that route is deployed, it falls back to `index.json`, which has per-pack counts but no test list.
- `catalog-history.json`, the number of checks at each release tag, from git (Pester `It` blocks before 3.0, native test files from 3.0 on).

The daily build-website run refreshes both, so new community checks show up within a day.

## Notes

- The per-test community listing needs the `catalog.json` route on the packs site (a separate change in the packs repo, not yet deployed). Without it the counts are right but community checks don't appear as catalog rows.
- Every test counts once; shims and checks that another suite also runs are not merged.

EOF

content.text:
I pushed fixes to [maester365/maester#2728](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2728) (commit `f372c8e`) for the failing Codacy check and CodeRabbit's five inline comments. CI is running again on the new commit.

**Codacy:** it flagged the pattern that recognises release tags in `catalog-history.mjs` as unsafe. I replaced it with a plain split-and-check, which gives the same 12 releases as before.

**CodeRabbit's five comments:**
- A pack listed without its tests no longer stops the catalog from being built.
- One bad entry from packs.maester.cloud (no code or name) is now skipped, instead of dropping every community pack.
- If the saved community-packs file is damaged, the build now continues without community packs instead of failing.
- When the catalog selection mixes community and shipped pack checks, the note under the run command now names the community packs that the command leaves out.
- The "From 106 checks in Maester 0.1…" sentence is now hidden when there's no release history.

I replied to each of the five threads and resolved them.

**Left as is:** CodeRabbit's summary also pointed out that community packs only appear at "Today" on the chart, so the curve jumps at the end. That's deliberate, because packs.maester.cloud keeps no history of community packs yet. That note isn't on a thread, so I didn't reply to it.

I checked both pages locally: the homepage section renders, and the catalog lists the 618 community checks.

CodeRabbit left three new comments on [maester365/maester#2728](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2728). I fixed one and pushed it as `4abca96`; I didn't change anything for the other two.

- **Fixed:** the build now checks that `community-packs.json` has a list of packs. If it doesn't, the build warns and continues without community packs. I replied on that thread and resolved it.
- **Not changed, the note under the run command:** CodeRabbit wants a note under the run command whenever community checks are on screen, including on the default All checks list. That would bring back the long note you asked me to remove. I replied with that reason and left the thread open for you or CodeRabbit to close.
- **Not changed, the product bars:** CodeRabbit says the "Checks by product" bars leave out community checks when the site has only each pack's total. That only happens until the `catalog.json` route ([jozrahq/maester-cloud-packs#15](https://github.com/jozrahq/maester-cloud-packs/pull/15)) is deployed. After that, every community check is in the bars. This comment wasn't on a thread, so I didn't reply.

input.recap: I reviewed the maester.dev homepage against apple.com. All 15 sections share one white background, the same 56px padding and the same left-aligned heading, so nothing marks where one ends and the next begins. Nothing is changed yet; the plan regroups them into 8 chapters, each on a coloured tile.
input.ask: How should I start the homepage redesign?

content.text:
## Critical review

**1. Nothing separates one section from the next.** I measured the page. All 15 sections below the hero have no background of their own, the same 56px top padding, and the same pattern: a small mono label, a left-aligned 31–36px heading and a paragraph. Your eye never gets a "new chapter" cue, so it reads as one long document.

Apple does the opposite. Every message sits on its own tile, which is a solid surface alternating black and light grey (`#f5f5f7`). Each tile is about 692px tall, with a 12px white gap between tiles, and that gap is the separator. Below the big tiles comes a two-up grid of smaller tiles with the same 12px gap.

**2. Fifteen sections and no story.** The order doesn't build an argument:
- The podcast ("Watch and listen") is 5th, before you've shown what Maester checks.
- The Zero Trust Assessment appears in the hero, the screenshot tabs, Coverage, its own section and Packs.
- Packs are split across the growth section, the ZTA section and the Packs section, while "Write your own" sits apart from them.
- The Maester Cloud upsell sits between Sponsors and Community.

A visitor can't tell what the page wants them to do.

**3. The headings are all the same size.** The page title is 61px and every section heading is 31–36px, left-aligned and in the same style. Apple makes each tile's heading the biggest thing on it (56px on the full-width tiles, 40px on the half tiles), centred, with one line beneath it and two buttons at most.

**4. The same facts repeat.** "890 checks" is in the hero, the stats band and the growth section, and the ZTA story is told three times. Every repeat makes the page longer and weakens each section.

**5. The calls to action don't match.** Some sections end in a button, some in a text link, some in a code block and some in nothing.

## Plan

**One tile component, three tones.** Add a `HomeSection.astro` with a `tone` setting: white, grey or ink (dark). It would give every section:
- full width, or a rounded tile with 12px gaps between tiles
- a centred header: label, a 48–56px heading, one sentence underneath, and at most two buttons
- a minimum height, so every chapter feels like a screen of its own

Dark mode gets matching versions of each tone.

**Cut 15 sections down to 8 chapters**, alternating tones so each boundary is visible:

| # | Chapter | Built from | Tone |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | What Maester is | Hero + report screenshot | white |
| 2 | Proof | Stats band | grey strip |
| 3 | The checks | Growth chart + Coverage (frameworks) | ink |
| 4 | How it works | Video + Automate (run it every day) | grey |
| 5 | Extend it | ZTA + Packs + Write your own, as three half-width tiles | white |
| 6 | 3.0 | What's new, as one short tile linking to the launch post | ink |
| 7 | Community | Contributors + podcast + sponsors | grey |
| 8 | Next step | Maester Cloud as the closing band | ink |

**Trim the copy.** Give each fact one home: the check count lives in chapter 3 and ZTA in chapter 5. Each tile carries one heading, one sentence and its buttons, and the detail moves to the linked pages.

**Use one button style everywhere:** a solid button for the main action and a text link for the second.

**Check the result** at desktop, tablet and phone widths, in light and dark mode, and make sure nothing still blends into its neighbour.

content.text:
The mock is open in the browser pane at http://localhost:3200/home-mock.html. Use the **Theme** button in the header to switch between light and dark.

**What changed from today's page:**
- **Every section has its own background.** Sections alternate between white, light grey and near-black, with a 12px gap between them, so you can always see where one ends and the next begins. In dark mode the near-black sections take a dark red tint so they still stand apart from the black page.
- **Every section is laid out the same way:** a small label, a large centred heading, one sentence, then one red button and one text link.
- **A chapter bar in the header** (What it is · The checks · How it works · Extend · 3.0 · Community) highlights the chapter you're in as you scroll, so the page's structure is visible at a glance.
- **The 15 sections are now 8:**
  1. The hero, with the report preview.
  2. The stats strip.
  3. **The checks**: the growth chart and checks by product, with the frameworks as chips.
  4. **How it works**: the video, the four steps, and the places it runs.
  5. **Extend**: a wide Packs tile, plus two half-width tiles for "Write your own" and Zero Trust.
  6. **3.0**: three short points and a link to the launch post.
  7. **Community**: the podcast, sponsors and contributing.
  8. **Maester Cloud** as the closing section.
- **Each fact appears once.** The check count lives in "The checks", and the Zero Trust story in "Extend".

I checked it at desktop and phone widths, in both themes, and nothing overflows sideways.

**Caveats:**
- The copy and numbers come from the current page, but the report preview, video, avatars and sponsor logos are placeholders.
- The mock file is in `website/public/` only so the dev server can show it. It isn't committed and shouldn't be. A copy is also at `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-merill--claude-spares-spare-qE5EWv/9948f473-294e-4c13-b6e3-fb178c50639e/scratchpad/home-mock.html`.

The site builds, nothing is committed (branch feat/website-home-chapters), and Microsoft's own Zero Trust report isn't in the demo yet.
input.ask: How should the Zero Trust report with the Sankey chart get into the demo?

content.text:
The new homepage and the live demo are working on the local site (http://localhost:3200, open in the browser pane). Microsoft's own Zero Trust report, the one with the Sankey chart, isn't in the demo yet: my build that included it was blocked (details below). I checked the page at desktop and phone widths and in both themes, and the site builds without errors. Nothing is committed; the work is on a new branch, `feat/website-home-chapters`, made from main.

**Homepage**
- The page now follows the mock: eight chapters on alternating white, grey and dark tiles with gaps between them. Each has a centred heading, one sentence, and a red button plus a text link.
- A chapter bar under the site header highlights the chapter you're in as you scroll.

**Live demo**
- The report preview at the top has a new **Live demo** tab. It loads the real report with the Contoso sample data, and visitors can click through all of it.
- **Try the live demo** in the hero opens that tab. **See the plan**, in the Zero Trust tile, opens the demo straight at the Zero Trust plan.
- Two new buttons sit at the right of the tab bar: **full screen** and **open in a new tab**. Full screen works for the still views and the live demo alike. If a browser refuses full screen (iPhone Safari), the button opens the report in a new tab instead.
- The automatic slideshow cycles through the still views only and never switches to the live demo by itself.
- I couldn't test full screen with a real click: clicks in the preview pane don't reach the button. Calling the button directly runs the right code: it asks for full screen and, when that's refused, opens the report in a new tab.

**New report views**
- I recaptured all the views, so they now show the blade layout, where the sidebar folds to icons and a pack's or framework's own menu opens beside it.
- Two new views show the Zero Trust plan: the swimlane board and the table.
- Until now the demo showed only the generic pack menu. It now carries the Zero Trust pack's own menu and the plan, using the same sample data as the report's dev server. To make that repeatable I:
  - added `report/scripts/export-demo-data.mjs`, which writes that sample data;
  - extended `website/scripts/build-demo-report.mjs` to embed attachments.

**What's missing: Microsoft's own Zero Trust report**
- The only copy I found is `ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html` in the maester-cloud repo. It comes from the real demo tenant and names real people. Among others: Manoj Kesana, Afif Ahmed, Shonali Balakrishna and Wilna Rossouw.
- The demo build now replaces every name and address it knows about and fails if any is left. Even so, the safety check blocked me from reading that file into the public demo.
- Once the report is added, rerun the capture script. That adds a "Zero Trust report" view to the showcase automatically.

There are two ways to add it:
- **You run the build with that file:** the command is below. The build fails if it finds a known name, but please look over the report before it goes public. People named only in plain text, not in links or addresses, may not be on my list.
- **Use a clean tenant:** generate a fresh Zero Trust Assessment report against a tenant with no real people in it.

```bash
cd website && node scripts/build-demo-report.mjs ../report/dist/index.html /tmp/maester-demo/results.json --attach "zero-trust-workshop=/tmp/maester-demo/zero-trust-workshop.json" --attach "Zero Trust Assessment=$HOME/github/maester-cloud/scripts/local-samples/zt/ZeroTrustAssessmentReport.html"
```

The two `/tmp/maester-demo` files come from `report/scripts/export-demo-data.mjs`. Run `cd report && node scripts/export-demo-data.mjs /tmp/maester-demo` first; the report template must already be built (`npm run build` in `report/`).

input.ask: Soften the homepage's colours and type?

content.text:
It isn't a different white. The homepage already uses Apple's light tones: white (`#fff`) and the light grey (`#f5f5f7`). The harsh feel comes from the black sections and the headline type. The Apple values below are from memory of apple.com's stylesheet; I didn't check the live site.

**1. Too many flat black sections.** Four sections are near-black (`#0b0b0d`): the checks, "Write your own", Maester Cloud, and the dark report preview inside the hero. They hold only text, so you see a lot of very dark area right next to white. On apple.com the dark sections are mostly product photos, so the eye reads the picture and not the black. Apple also keeps dark sections rare and uses white and light grey for most of the page. Our rhythm flips between white, black and grey every section, which is the "stark" part.

**2. Too much contrast in the text.**

| | Ours | Apple |
|---|---|---|
| Text on dark | `#fafafa` | `#f5f5f7` |
| Text on light | `#18181b` (a cool grey-black) | `#1d1d1f` (a neutral grey-black) |
| Secondary text | `#52525b` | `#6e6e73` / `#86868b` |

Apple's grey text is noticeably lighter, which softens every paragraph.

**3. Heavier, tighter headlines.**
- **Weight:** ours are Inter at weight 700. Apple uses SF Pro Display at weight 600.
- **Letter spacing:** ours is `-0.03em`. Apple's is about `-0.005em` on section headlines and `-0.015em` on the hero. That makes ours roughly twice as tight.
- **Font:** at large sizes, Inter's regular cut looks wider and blunter than a display cut. Inter Display, its large-size cut, is closer to SF.
- **Result:** bold, condensed-looking headlines on flat black come across as shouting rather than calm.

**4. The red button on black.** The `#d22c31` pill on near-black is the highest-contrast thing on the page, and it appears in several sections. Apple keeps colour for links and small buttons on light backgrounds.

**What I'd change:**
1. Keep one or two dark sections at most: Maester Cloud, and maybe the checks section, which has the chart to fill it. Make the others light grey.
2. Use a softer dark (`#161617`) with `#f5f5f7` text and `#86868b` for secondary text.
3. Change the light-theme text to `#1d1d1f` and the secondary text to `#6e6e73`.
4. Set headlines to weight 600 with letter spacing of about `-0.015em`, and switch to Inter Display if the site can load it.

content.text:
There's now a pricing page at `/pricing`, and the homepage has a Maester vs Maester Cloud comparison. Both work on the dev server at desktop and phone widths, with no sideways scrolling; I haven't rerun the full site build, and nothing is committed.

**Pricing page** ([pricing.astro](src/pages/pricing.astro))
- The headline is "Maester is free. Wherever you run it." Below it are four cards:

| Card | Price | Main point | Button goes to |
|---|---|---|---|
| Your desktop | Free | Every check, pack and the report; your data stays on your machine | Install guide |
| GitHub Actions | Free | Daily scheduled runs, reports kept with each run, email or Teams alerts | GitHub Actions guide |
| Automation | Free | Azure Automation, Azure DevOps, Container Apps, GitLab, Bitbucket; Bicep and Terraform templates | Automation guides |
| Maester Cloud | From $99 / month | Runs securely in Azure, simplified deployment, run history, drift and alerts across tenants | maester.cloud/pricing |

- $99 a month is the lowest price on maester.cloud/pricing today, for the Self-Hosted plan.
- Maester Cloud is a dark card so it stands out from the three free ones.
- A note under the cards says the checks are the same in every option and that Cloud subscriptions fund the maintainers.
- "Pricing" is now in the site header, before "Maester Cloud ↗", and in the footer under Product.

**Homepage comparison**
- It replaces the old Maester Cloud section near the bottom, so it's the last section before Sponsors. It is also a new "Maester Cloud" entry in the chapter bar.
- The heading is "Same checks. You choose who runs them." It's followed by a side-by-side table:

| | Maester (free, open source) | Maester Cloud (from $99 / month) |
|---|---|---|
| Checks, packs and report | Every one | The same, every one |
| Where it runs | Your desktop, GitHub Actions or your own pipelines | Securely in Azure |
| Setup | You install, schedule and store the reports | Simplified deployment, nothing to script |
| Run history | One report per run | Every run, for every tenant |
| Drift and alerts | Email and Teams alerts you set up | Across tenants, built in |
| Price | Free | From $99 a month |

- The buttons are **Explore Maester Cloud** and **Compare pricing**, which goes to the new page.

The "hundreds" turned out to be community packs, not tests in Maester itself. - **Packs intro:** It now adds: "The community's CIS Intune benchmark packs add 579 device checks on their own, one for each setting."
- **Pack cards:** These are now the Zero Trust Assessment pack plus the three largest community packs: CIS Windows 11 Intune L1, Edge and macOS. Each card links to its pack page and names its publisher. They used to be three hand-picked cards (Zero Trust Assessment, Least Privileged MSGraph, RKSolutions Intune Anomalies); those two community packs drop off the homepage but stay on packs.maester.cloud.
- **Updates with the catalog:** The cards, the 579 and the 618 all come from the pack catalog at build time, so they change as packs are added or grow.

Maester is an open-source security test framework for Microsoft 365, and it has a hosted product called Maester Cloud. The "Maester my Microsoft 365" listing on the Microsoft Marketplace is a separate packaged offering that bundles Maester with configuration tracking, so the search doesn't show it as the SaaS itself.

- **Maester (the framework):** The official site describes it as the open-source security test framework for Microsoft 365, Entra, Azure and Active Directory. It is PowerShell-based and runs Pester tests, and the current docs describe Install-Module Maester as the install step. The docs note that the site covers the 3.0 preview, which differs from 2.x in places.
- **Maester Cloud (the SaaS):** This is the hosted layer. It sends Maester and Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment results to a portal you run in your own Azure subscription, keeping 5+ years of tenant history, highlighting drift between runs, and alerting you the moment it changes. It also states that your data never leaves your tenant.
- **Maester my Microsoft 365 (Marketplace listing):** This is a simplified, user-friendly solution that runs directly in your own environment. It lists 300+ built-in checks, including those from the Entra ID Security Config Analyzer.

Sources differ on the check count. The official Maester site and third-party write-ups cite figures such as 360+ built-in tests, so the number depends on the version.

- **Maester** is an open-source security test framework for Microsoft 365, Entra, Azure and Active Directory. It runs 892 built-in checks across CIS, CISA SCuBA, EIDSCA and ORCA, and the Zero Trust Assessment pack ships with Maester and runs Microsoft's assessment in its own PowerShell session.
- **Maester Cloud** is the commercial layer. It sends Maester and Microsoft Zero Trust Assessment results to a portal you run in your own Azure subscription. The search didn't turn up a native integration between Maester and an MSP platform. Maester is a standalone, open-source PowerShell tool, and the MSP-specific material is about running it yourself across tenants.

- **What it does:** Maester runs security tests against a Microsoft 365 tenant and reports which configurations pass or fail. Found an incorrect configuration? Create a new test to ensure it doesn't happen again.
- **MSP relevance:** Its documentation says Maester supports running security tests across multiple Microsoft 365 tenants and viewing the results in a single HTML report. One MSP-focused review describes it as particularly valuable for MSPs managing multiple Microsoft 365 tenants, offering automated security assessments and compliance validation at scale.
- **Custom tests:** It is built on Pester, a PowerShell testing framework, so custom tests are written in that framework.
- **Basic workflow:** Setup involves installing the module, creating a tests folder, and running Connect-Maester signs in to the tenant, and Invoke-Maester runs the tests.
- **Version differences:** Sources disagree on test counts, which likely reflects different Maester versions. One recent post says Maester 3.0 replaces Pester with its own test engine, adds drift tracking between runs, skips tests the tenant isn't licensed for, and maps tests to frameworks like NIST and CIS, and describes about 700 checks. Older sources cite 140+ or 280+ tests, and the 3.0 engine change makes the Pester description outdated for current versions.

Searching for the specific MSP platform name alongside Maester may turn up an actual connector if one exists.

## Introduction to Maester

---
title: Community projects
description: Open-source projects and commercial products that build on Maester, from deployment templates to managed services.
---

Maester is open source, so other people build on it. This page lists the projects and products we know of that run Maester or use its results, so you can find one that fits how you work.

We don't review or endorse these projects, and we haven't tested them ourselves. Check what each one asks for, such as permissions, data storage and pricing, before you use it with your tenant. To add your project or correct an entry, edit this page with the link at the bottom and open a pull request.

## Open source

### Run Maester on a schedule

| Project | By | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [DriftMaester](https://github.com/jflieben/DriftMaester) | Jos Lieben | Deploys Maester to Azure Automation with one command. It runs on a schedule, keeps the history in Blob Storage, flags drift and regressions, and emails the report. |
| [azd-maester](https://github.com/nathanmcnulty/azd-maester) | Nathan McNulty | Azure Developer CLI templates that run Maester with managed identities on [Azure Automation](https://github.com/nathanmcnulty/azd-maester-azureautomation), [Azure Functions](https://github.com/nathanmcnulty/azd-maester-functionapp), [Azure Container Apps jobs](https://github.com/nathanmcnulty/azd-maester-containerappjob) or [Azure DevOps](https://github.com/nathanmcnulty/azd-maester-azuredevops). |
| [Kickstarter: Maester & UTCM Dashboard](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/kickstarter-maester-and-utcm) | Fortytwo | An Azure Web App that runs Maester daily and lets you browse the reports by date. It adds drift detection through Unified Tenant Configuration Management (UTCM), baselines, webhooks and a remediation board. |
| [Maester-O365](https://github.com/adrian207/Maester-O365) | Adrian Johnson | A GitHub template that runs Maester every day with workload identity federation, so no secret is stored. One script sets up the app and secrets. |
| [terraform-azure-maester-deployment](https://github.com/hlokensgard/terraform-azure-maester-deployment) | Henrik Løkensgard | A Terraform module that deploys Maester to Azure Automation, with an optional web app to view the report. |

### Assessments that include Maester

| Project | By | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [GxAssessMS](https://github.com/Guardantix/gxassessms) | Guardantix | Runs ScubaGear, Maester, Monkey365, Prowler and other tools from one config file. It merges their overlapping findings and writes one Word report. |
| [M365Assessment](https://github.com/patramsden/M365Assessment) | Pat Ramsden | Runs Maester, then its own Conditional Access, Entra ID, Copilot data security and Purview reviews, and writes an HTML dashboard and a Word or PDF report. |

### Tests and packs

[Maester Packs](https://packs.maester.cloud) lists the community packs you can install with `Install-MtPack`. Collections of custom tests include:

- [Custom-Maester-Tests](https://github.com/DevClate/Custom-Maester-Tests) by Clayton Tyger
- [maester-copilot-tests](https://github.com/LukeEvansTech/maester-copilot-tests), Microsoft 365 Copilot checks by Luke Evans
- [entra-ca-templates](https://github.com/LukeEvansTech/entra-ca-templates), Conditional Access policies as code checked with Maester, by Luke Evans

## Commercial products and services

| Product | By | What it is | Price |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Maester Cloud](https://maester.cloud) | Jozra, from Maester's creator | Runs Maester and Microsoft's Zero Trust Assessment in your own Azure subscription. It keeps the run history for every tenant, tracks findings and drift, and sends alerts. Also on the [Microsoft Marketplace](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/jozra.maester-cloud). | From $99 a month ([pricing](https://maester.cloud/pricing)) |
| [Maester my Microsoft 365](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/fortytwoio.maester) | Fortytwo | An Azure application on the Microsoft Marketplace that deploys Maester and UTCM monitoring into your own tenant. It includes run history, a remediation board and configuration baselines. | Free, according to [Fortytwo](https://fortytwo.io/marketplace-products/maester-my-microsoft-365/) |
| [Coldbyte Security](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/coldbyteas1788469511939.coldbyte-security) | Coldbyte | Runs Maester and the Zero Trust Assessment every day in a deployment in your Azure subscription. It explains findings and security events in Teams and, on the Full plan, applies fixes you approve. | From $5 per user a month, plus Azure consumption |
| [Mobula](https://mobula.cloud) | Mobula Cloud | A platform for managed service providers that scans customers' Azure, Microsoft 365, Entra ID, GitHub and Fabric. It shows Maester results and what changed since the last scan, including in a [Microsoft 365 Copilot connector](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/WA200012816). | Mobula subscription |
| [TestimoX](https://testimox.com/maester/) | Evotec | An Active Directory assessment platform. It runs its assessment once and passes signed results to Maester, which shows them in the Maester report. | The Maester integration is free; [paid tiers](https://testimox.com/pricing/) add more |
| [Security Guardian for Microsoft 365](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/sentineltechnologiesinc.sti-maester-managed) | Sentinel Technologies | A managed service: monthly security posture reports against CISA SCuBA and CIS guidance, and monthly calls with engineers who review the findings. | From $18,000 a year |

input.recap: All the review feedback on PR 2737 is fixed in commit ab287e410 and pushed. All seven inline threads have a reply and are resolved. The site builds, and the homepage showed no console errors at phone width.

content.text:
I fixed the review comments on [maester365/maester#2737](https://github.com/maester365/maester/pull/2737) in one commit, `ab287e410`, and pushed it. All seven inline threads have a reply and are resolved. The site builds, and the homepage loads at phone width with no console errors.

**Demo report scripts**
- `build-demo-report.mjs`:
  - The tenant ID is now replaced whatever its case.
  - Before, a sample without a tenant ID crashed the build; now that step is skipped.
  - Two attachments that would get the same ID now stop the build with an error.
- `capture-demo-report.mjs`: if a view is skipped, its old screenshot is deleted so the homepage doesn't show it.

**Homepage**
- The report preview only appears if at least one view was captured. Before, having none crashed the page's script.
- On phones, the full-screen and open buttons now stay at the end of the scrolling tab bar instead of being pushed off-screen.

**Wording**

| Where | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Pricing card | "Run it securely in Azure." | "Run it in your own Azure subscription." The card body says the $99 plan deploys into your own subscription. |
| Data bullet | "Your data never leaves the Azure region you choose" | "Your report data never leaves the Azure region you choose" |

The homepage comparison table has the same two changes. Both match maester.cloud: $99 is the self-hosted plan, and its privacy statement keeps only customer data in your chosen region. Account and billing data can be processed elsewhere.

**Community projects page**
- **DriftMaester:** its licence needs the author's written consent for commercial use. I left it second, as you asked, but labelled it "source-available" with a link to the licence.
- **TestimoX:** the entry now says its Maester adapter isn't published yet.

None of the comments asked for anything beyond fixing the PR.
